skill.name: distill
skill.description: Simplifies interface designs by removing clutter, reducing choices, and keeping elements that support the primary user goal.
skill.summary: Simplify interface designs while preserving essential user goals and accessibility.
skill.author: pbakaus

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a false positive. SKILL.md line 61 tells the model to remove duplicated design copy. It does not request system, environment, host, network, or filesystem reconnaissance.

static_findings.snippet: - **Remove redundancy**: If it's said elsewhere, don't repeat it here

finding_verdicts.reason: The line is a design instruction to remove repeated content. It does not ask for system, environment, host, network, or filesystem reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: Complex interfaces slow decisions and hide the main user goal. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to remove clutter, clarify hierarchy, and preserve needed functionality.
actual_capabilities: Identifies interface complexity from redundant actions, excessive variation, and unclear hierarchy.
Defines one primary user goal before recommending simplification.
Suggests progressive disclosure, consolidation, and removal of nonessential elements.
Reviews visual, layout, interaction, content, and code-level complexity.
Checks whether changes preserve accessibility, essential information, and task completion.
limitations: Does not generate production code by itself; it guides design and implementation choices.
Requires product and user context to decide what is essential.
May ask for clarification when goals, constraints, or existing design context are unclear.
Cannot validate outcomes without review, testing, or user feedback.

use_cases.title: Refine Busy Product Screens
use_cases.description: Find redundant UI elements and reduce competing actions while keeping the main task clear.

use_cases.title: Reduce UI Implementation Complexity
use_cases.description: Simplify nested layouts, repeated components, and unnecessary variants before building or refactoring.

use_cases.title: Clarify Feature Scope
use_cases.description: Separate essential user value from optional ideas before a design review or sprint plan.

prompt_templates.title: Simplify a Screen
prompt_templates.prompt: Use distill on the current screen. Identify the primary user goal, list unnecessary elements, and suggest the smallest useful simplification plan.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single interface

prompt_templates.title: Reduce Interaction Choices
prompt_templates.prompt: Use distill for the target feature. Compare all actions and options, then recommend what to keep, combine, hide, or remove.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a Complex Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use distill on the target workflow. Map the essential path, remove unnecessary steps, preserve accessibility, and document tradeoffs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced simplification of a multi-step experience

prompt_templates.title: Audit Design and Code Complexity
prompt_templates.prompt: Use distill to review the target across layout, content, visual hierarchy, and component structure. Produce prioritized changes and verification checks.

output_examples.input: A dashboard has six primary buttons, repeated status text, nested cards, and three sidebar panels.
output_examples.output: Primary goal: review account health. Keep one main action, merge repeated status copy, flatten nested cards, and move side panels behind clear entry points.

output_examples.input: A checkout flow asks for account creation, promo codes, shipping details, gift options, and surveys on one page.
output_examples.output: Essential path: complete purchase. Defer surveys, collapse optional gift details, keep promo codes secondary, and show account creation after payment.

output_examples.input: A settings page uses many colors, mixed typography, repeated explanations, and separate buttons for similar actions.
output_examples.output: Simplification plan: standardize type, reduce accent colors, remove repeated copy, group related settings, and expose one primary save action.

best_practices: Start by naming one primary user goal before removing anything.
Preserve accessibility, required information, and recovery paths during simplification.
Document removed complexity so product teams can review tradeoffs later.
anti_patterns: Do not remove features only to make the screen look minimal.
Do not hide essential decisions behind unclear controls or unlabeled icons.
Do not simplify complex domains without understanding user risk and compliance needs.

faq.question: What does this skill help simplify?
faq.answer: It helps simplify interface structure, visual hierarchy, interaction choices, content, and component complexity.

faq.question: Can it remove product features automatically?
faq.answer: No. It recommends simplification choices and asks for context when feature value is unclear.

faq.question: Does it support accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. The instructions warn against sacrificing labels, ARIA, required information, or clear hierarchy.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it before design review, UI refactoring, scope reduction, or cleanup of a crowded workflow.

faq.question: Does it work with codebases?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide removal of unused code, deep component nesting, and excessive variants.

faq.question: What context improves results?
faq.answer: Provide the target user, primary goal, constraints, screenshots, current UI, and any must-keep requirements.
